title: The Test of the True Disciple (TE)
summary: A guru claims his disciples have mastered all desires. Birbal places a plate of fresh mangoes before them in a dark room to test their discipline. [TE]
full_text:
A proud ascetic named Swami Chinmayananda arrived in Agra with fifty saffron-clad disciples. The guru boasted before Emperor Akbar: 'My disciples have conquered all worldly passions! They know neither hunger, nor lust, nor anger, nor greed! They are living saints!'

Akbar was deeply impressed, but Birbal remained skeptical. 'Sire, conquering human desire is the work of a lifetime. Let us test their mastery tonight.'

Birbal invited the guru and his disciples to stay in a palace hall. That evening, Birbal arranged for the disciples to be served a very light dinner of plain boiled rice.

Around midnight, when the disciples were sleeping fitfully on their mats with rumbling stomachs, Birbal quietly placed three large brass platters laden with fragrant, ripe Alphonso mangoes—sliced, chilled, and dripping with sweet nectar—in the center of the dark hall.

Birbal announced softly from the doorway: 'Holy brothers, these mangoes are an imperial offering. However, by your master's vows, you must not touch them until the morning sun rises!'

Birbal extinguished the lamps and closed the door.

An hour later, in the pitch-black darkness, sounds of soft rustling and chewing echoed through the hall: *Slurp... munch... smack!*

The next morning, when the doors opened and sunlight flooded the room, the brass platters were completely licked clean!

Moreover, every single disciple had yellow mango pulp and sticky juice smeared across his chin, cheeks, and saffron robes! Each disciple looked at his brothers in horrified embarrassment.

Birbal turned to the boastful guru with a polite bow:

'Swamiji, your disciples may have renounced worldly wealth, but when the lights went out, the sweet mango of temptation proved mightier than all their vows!

'True mastery of the mind cannot be claimed with proud words; it is tested in the dark when no one is watching.'

The humbled guru bowed his head, apologized for his vanity, and departed with his disciples to practice genuine humility.
